So you're Rosa's grandchild! I'm Oona. Your grandmother and I go back a long, long way.
I've just come from a sunny valley in the south, where cherry trees grow between old stone walls.
I brought something special from there. But first, let me see how you look after this orchard.
When Rosa and I were girls, we planted the very first tree of this orchard together. A Sweet Cherry, right where the path bends.
She said one day this orchard would be full of trees from all over the world. I think it's time.
I'm back! This time I went high into the mountains, to a garden where monks keep silkworms.
Silkworms eat mulberry leaves, you know. And there I found a mulberry as white as snow.
But first, show me you remember the trick I taught you.
Rosa was the one who taught me to graft, you know. Her hands were always green with sap.
I was hopeless at first. She just laughed and said: trees forgive, if you try again.
This time I travelled north, to a village by a dark lake. They grow a Morello there that's almost black.
The villagers sell it at a market that never seems to close. Clever traders, all of them.
Let me see if you can trade as well as you grow.
Rosa and I used to carry baskets of cherries to the town market. She always sold more than me.
Her secret? She talked to every buyer as if they were an old friend.
My longest journey yet — far north, where the snow never quite melts.
There I saw sour cherries blooming at the very edge of the snow. Pale pink, as if made of frost.
A tree like that needs many hands. Have you called your family yet?
Do you know why I started travelling? I promised Rosa I'd bring the world's seeds back to her orchard.
Golden, Snow, Midnight, Frost... and there are so many more out there.
Keep the orchard growing, dear. I'll keep walking.
Your trees are heavy with fruit. Go on, pick them.
Bruno at the stall buys fruit. Sell him ten.
Bruno sells saplings too. Plant two — anywhere you like.
Now the hardest part of gardening: patience.
Four Sweet Cherry trees — then you're ready for my gift.
Has my golden sapling grown up yet? Let's see.
Take a cutting from your golden tree. Gently!
Now graft it onto a Sweet Cherry tree. Watch it change.
Mulberries are soft — pick them while they're sweet.
Three Mulberry trees, and the white one will feel at home.
Morellos first. Pick them dark and ripe.
Watch Bruno's prices — they change every day.
Sell too much of one fruit and the price drops. Mix them!
More Morello trees — the dark one likes company.
Earn three hundred at the market. Then it's yours.
Rosa's children and grandchildren — invite one of them.
Let them work the orchard too. Everyone has a gift.
Sour cherries make the best jam — Rosa's favourite.
Grow three more. The orchard is filling up!
Three Sour Cherry trees — the frost one will be happy here.
